## Recurring Template

A transaction that repeats: `templateId`, `name`, `docKind` (invoice, bill or journal), `party` (the customer ID for an invoice, the vendor ID for a bill), `type` (scheduled, reminder or unscheduled, as QuickBooks has them), `schedule` (the catalog's `RecurringPatternField`), `daysInAdvance`, `nextDate`, `lastRunDate`, `runCount`, `paused`, and the body: `memo`, `taxCode`, and `saleLines`, `billLines` or `entryLines` by kind (`preparer` for a journal entry). `totalMinor` adds up a run.

```ts
import { RecurringTemplate, nextRunAfter } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/accounting/ledger-recurring';
```

`nextRunAfter(schedule, date, runCount)` gives the run after a date, using the maintenance cluster's recurrence functions; BXL has no calendar arithmetic, so the desk works the date out and the operation checks it.

### Operations
- `advance`: on a scheduled or reminder template that isn't paused, takes the `runDate` (which must be `nextDate`) and the next date (after it, or null when the schedule has run out), and records the run.
- `ran`: records a run made by hand (an unscheduled template, or one run early), without moving the schedule.
- `pause` / `resume`.

The desk sends `advance` or `ran` in one batch with the run's draft (Customer `enterInvoice`, Ledger `enterBill` or `enterJournal`), numbered with the template ID and the run date, so a run can't make two drafts. Its Recurring page runs every scheduled template that's due, catching up missed runs one at a time; reminders show as due on Home; any document's drawer can make a monthly template from it.

### Non-goals
Runs create drafts; nothing posts on its own. No custom recurrence rules, and nothing runs without someone opening the desk.

### Example
`RecurringTemplate/RT-RENT-EASTSIDE`, the roastery rent bill on the first of each month, drafted five days early.
